checklist.evidence: Reviewed all 32 paths in specs/verifications/e06-review-round8-source.json, the three E06 stories, settled scope/threat model, and PLAN.md lines 1-45 only. E05 remains parked; no earlier review/runtime/handoff evidence was used.

src/acp_profiles.rs, src/cli.rs and src/daemon.rs distinguish named profiles from raw command launches. Missing profiles/executables and conflicting launch forms fail explicitly; profile discovery excludes argv/environment.

src/projects.rs and src/acp_profiles.rs validate profile count, identifiers, labels, argv and defaults before accepting configuration. Failed configuration persistence/validation retains the previous usable configuration.

src/acp_profiles.rs resolves only absolute executables or bare commands in absolute PATH directories, retaining the invocation path rather than canonicalizing away symlink identity. src/acp.rs uses Command::new plus args, not shell interpolation. tests/acp/profiles.rs covers absolute and PATH aliases.

src/acp/settings.rs bounds requested settings and rejects unknown fields/invalid identifiers. src/acp_profiles.rs parses explicit option JSON without delimiter splitting and rejects duplicate keys; CLI/native tests preserve IDs and choices containing commas and equals signs.

src/acp/settings.rs validates raw advertised metadata before permissive typed decoding can discard malformed entries. Duplicate option/choice IDs are rejected; ambiguous semantic categories fail rather than selecting an arbitrary option; explicit option IDs remain distinct.

src/acp.rs configure_next/apply and src/acp/settings.rs next/acknowledge retain the active original setter until its matching RPC succeeds. Configuration setters require value-confirming responses; later startup changes are checked against previously acknowledged settings before readiness.

Configuration projections separate requested, reported and unreported values and expose failed/changed states. src/tui/agent.rs and src/tui/launch.rs do not equate an absent default or selected model with a confirmed permission policy. tests/acp/omp.rs covers unreported defaults and rejected/unconfirmed settings.

checklist.area: Explicit CLI and native launch authority
checklist.evidence: src/cli.rs preserves explicit-controller automation while human launches use the original native attachment. src/tui/launch.rs requires deliberate submission, displays inherited defaults/unavailable executables, and sends selected project/profile/settings through the existing daemon operation.

src/daemon.rs acp_action authorizes the target and invokes broker commit under Authority::admit_acp. src/acp.rs rechecks owner generation, exact instance/connection/session tuple and duplicate call identity before publishing work; narrow src/control.rs references establish the shared revocation ordering point.

checklist.area: Force does not interrupt or kill
checklist.evidence: Ownership changes do not generate ACP prompt cancellation or process termination. tests/acp.rs and tests/acp/native/acceptance.rs retain original work/RPC/process identities across force and require an explicit acp-interrupt or acp-close for those effects.

Authority cancellation paths retain admitted ACP work and pending callbacks without rebinding them to the requester. tests/acp.rs covers cancellation before/after offer, stale controls/offers and subsequent deliberate reacquisition.

checklist.area: Conditional keep and external reacquisition policy
checklist.evidence: src/tui/control.rs retains original-connection view/activity/consent ordering. src/control.rs guards and native acceptance tests distinguish keep/withdraw from release/grant and require external policy to create a new attempt.

src/tui.rs routes native bytes, paste, literal prefix, application mouse and ACP actions through NativeControl/current grants. Observer keys, intercepted confirmations and mouse tails are consumed rather than queued for later replay; tests/pty_control/native.rs and tests/acp/native.rs exercise these routes.

checklist.area: Captured drafts and actions do not rebind
checklist.evidence: src/tui/agent.rs binds drafts/reviews/actions to the exact target, control generation and interaction revision. Authority or identity changes discard captures. Definite pre-admission rejection is distinguished from transport uncertainty; unknown requests are not automatically retried.

src/acp.rs parse_form/parse_permission retain original request IDs, session or outstanding-request scope, tool identity and exact offered options. Unsupported filesystem/terminal/URL methods receive errors rather than becoming new execution capabilities.

checklist.area: One response winner and typed cancellation IDs
checklist.evidence: src/acp.rs orders pending selection and $/cancel_request under the same state lock. Cancellation matches typed numeric/string RPC IDs, cannot overwrite an admitted winner and does not become a human answer or prompt interrupt. tests/acp/omp.rs and the e06s01 unit regression cover these distinctions.

src/acp.rs applies the distinct 4-KiB tool-call-ID bound to tool updates, session-scoped forms and permissions while preserving the complete identifier. Local setting/interaction/RPC identity and frame/content bounds remain separate.

src/acp.rs inert rendering and src/tui/agent.rs, src/tui/control.rs, src/tui/launch.rs and src/tui/view.rs sanitize control/bidirectional characters at rendering boundaries. Native hostile-rendering tests inspect escape sequences and title/clipboard effects rather than treating plain displayed text as sufficient proof.

src/acp.rs and src/daemon.rs distinguish content-enabled inspection from metadata/events. Provider error bodies, prompts, forms/selections and agent-supplied conversation content are not projected into the public ACP metadata path; tests/acp.rs and native acceptance tests assert this separation.

src/acp.rs bounds frames, ingress/egress bytes and counts, responders, interaction content/history, retained calls and live targets. Capacity checks precede publication; live responders are not evicted to admit more work, and a lifetime call slot remains available for explicit close.

src/acp.rs keeps accepted/submitted/write-failed delivery separate from original RPC completion and unknown application outcome. EOF, lost replies and unconfirmed selection never become proof of cancellation or application; tests/acp.rs covers retained unknown work and response-pipe failure.

src/acp.rs owns original endpoints, cancellation wakeup, child/session cleanup and joined pipe workers. Failed birth-qualified capture or incomplete endpoint/process cleanup remains failed/charged rather than being evicted as successful cleanup. Cleanup tests retain unrelated-process sentinels.

src/tui.rs Resume captures daemon and exact ACP instance/connection/session identity. Recovery validates the original target, permits only initial null-to-established session advancement, and ends on replacement/missing targets without same-name substitution or automatic relaunch.

checklist.area: Both native connection lifetimes are fenced
checklist.evidence: src/client.rs exposes connection-loss classification/liveness. src/tui/control.rs checks authority and observation sockets before dequeued work and again after compound claim observation, preventing a previously queued claim/launch from borrowing a newer observation lifetime.

checklist.area: Paused UI cannot lend stale queued authority
checklist.evidence: src/tui.rs uses conservative wall-clock pause detection; src/tui/control.rs checks the UI heartbeat before worker mutations and after blocking claim observation. Recovery-edge tests hold genuine responses across stopped UI/connection loss and assert no stale claim grant.

checklist.area: Recovery discards old input and authority
checklist.evidence: src/tui.rs creates fresh local UI/editor state and drains recovery input before readiness. NativeControl::recovered disables initial automatic acquisition; old controls, drafts, consent and claim UI are not imported into the new attachment.

src/tui/control.rs stop joins the old worker and preserves only an already parsed successful launch receipt. src/tui.rs records that exact target before subsequent snapshot validation and does not repeat the launch when the observation connection fails. tests/acp/native/recovery_edges.rs covers the loss boundaries.

Recovered attachment teardown attempts the existing controller close operation only after stopping/joining its worker. src/control.rs close guards refuse owner/pending-claim destruction, so cleanup does not release authority, cancel claims or silently acquire control; recovery-edge tests cover idle-observer accumulation.

src/tui.rs reconciles the actual painted/kernel terminal size after blocking setup and discarded recovery events, reapplying structural resize before declaring readiness. tests/pty_control/native.rs and tests/acp/native/recovery_edges.rs cover registration/selection resize and lost notifications.

checklist.area: Stock native behavior and historical limitations
checklist.evidence: tests/shell_races.rs, tests/pty_control/native.rs, README.md and CONVENTIONS.md preserve stock Zsh/native OMP distinctions. Existing unknown native application settlement continues to block safe handoff; explicit warned force is not represented as a repair or complete acceptance.

checklist.area: Dependencies, test boundaries and acceptance honesty
checklist.evidence: Reviewed src/lib.rs, Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, README.md, CHANGELOG.md and all frozen test sources. ACP schema is pinned at 1.12.0; synthetic fixtures are labeled non-provider evidence. tests/acp/native/omp_live.rs requires genuine same-agent callbacks/effects and external provider-budget evidence, but this ignored opt-in driver was not run and establishes no live PASS here.

summary: PASS for the independent static security gate: 32/32 checklist items passed, score 100*32/32 = 100. Reviewed all 32 frozen files (13 production, 11 test, 8 documentation/configuration), sealed E06 requirements and narrow unchanged authority controls. No evidence-backed Must-fix, Should-fix or optional security finding survived source-to-control/sink tracing. This is not E06 runtime or release acceptance.
limits: Read-only source analysis only. No edits, builds, lint, tests, formatters, shell/source or payload execution, provider/network calls, real auth/private retired fixture access, config/daemon/global operations or commits. No prior review/audit/repair/runtime report, saved handoff or execution log was read. Manifest hashes/branch identity were taken as the supplied sealed context, not independently recomputed. Installed OMP same-instance interoperability, actual native/API effects, runtime cleanup and live budget enforcement remain the parent's separate runtime gates. Historical unresolved native/application settlement and existing authorization counters/caps are unchanged; neither synthetic fixtures, ignored live tests nor this static PASS resolve them.
